noInherit.description: If true, the annotation is not inherited by mixins.

primaryShardsOverride.description:
This should be applied on a type and is used to specify the number of primary shards that should be created for
the index, provided that the index does not already exist on the search engine side. By default it is 1
If an index is already created, same SearchIndex will be used but number of primary shards will not change, only
reconstructing the index will change number of primary shards.

replicaShardsOverride.description:
This should be applied on a type and is used to specify the number of replica shards that should be created
for the index, provided that the index does not already exist on the search engine side. By default it is 1
If an index is already created, number of replica shards will change.

text.description:
This is a field-specific annotation and is used to override the data type of field to be text when persisting in
the search data store. By default, it's false and the fields {@link ValueType} will determine the data type when
persisting to the index data store.
Setting as text will ensure the field to be processed (i.e. tokenized, stemmed, etc.). Therefore, the inverted
index will use processed terms as opposed to the keyword
Ex: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
Stored as:
Term     | Count
the      | 2
quick    | 1
brown    | 1
fox      | 1
jumps    | 1
over     | 1
lazy     | 1
dog      | 1

keyword.description:
This is a field-specific annotation and is used for exact matching.

Setting a field as keyword will result in:
Ex: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
Stored as:
Term                                             | Count
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog      | 1

In this case, Query of 'fox' will not result in any hit, since it needs exact matching of the string, but
if override the type as text there will be hits.
Therefore, keyword is often used when exact matching (unique identifier) is required.
If both exact matching and tokenized query are required, multi-fields mapping supports mapping the field as
text and keyword. E.g @search(text=true, keyword=true)

name: Ann.Search
